steps.name: DESeq2 LRT for condition:time interaction
caveats: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. These are salmon gene-level counts as delivered with no quantification files and no average transcript length table, so the length offset is lost: state in the report that a shift in isoform usage can present as differential expression. If per-sample quant.sf files or an average-transcript-length-per-gene-and-sample table are supplied later, the import should be redone.

The interaction coefficient is a difference of two differences, so its standard error exceeds that of a main effect at the same replicate count. At 3 replicates per cell the interaction test has low power — keep it as the primary result, report the simple effects beside it at the same threshold, and do not loosen alpha to compensate.

At 3 replicates per group the test recovers only a minority of true effects, mostly those with large fold changes. A gene absent from the interaction list is NOT shown to have the same time profile in both conditions.

The power tools of record (RNASeqPower, PROPER) are not installed here; derive the power statement from the closed-form relation between depth, dispersion, fold change and alpha using the dispersions this fit estimates, and label it as an approximation.

plan.title: Treatment x time interaction DE across t0–t3
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a single gene-level count matrix (/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv, 12,000 genes x 25 columns — 24 sample columns plus a gene-id column) with a 24-row sample table (/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv: condition, time, time_hours). The design is 2 conditions x 4 time points (t0..t3) x 3 replicates = 24 samples, human cell line, raw counts. The research question — genes with a treatment-specific change over the four time points, beyond the shared time trend — is exactly the condition:time interaction. With 4 time points the interaction spans 3 coefficients, so a single Wald test cannot answer it; the DESeq2 likelihood ratio test of the full model ~ condition + time + condition:time against the reduced model ~ condition + time is the test of record (R-0014@a226). T1S1 runs blind-VST sample-structure QC first (PCA on the top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library sizes) so that an outlier or a time-dominated variance axis is known before the model. T1S2 fits the LRT, keeping DESeq2's median-of-ratios normalization inside the model and a minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=3 samples) so that independent filtering at alpha 0.05 does the rest. Because the interaction contrasts are not single model coefficients, T1S3 shrinks the per-time-point interaction log2 fold changes with ashr and clusters the significant genes by their treatment-minus-control trajectory across t1, t2, t3 relative to t0 — one fold change cannot describe a time-course gene. T1S4 assembles the report with the fit diagnostics, the p-value histogram, the simple effects beside the interaction result, and an explicit power statement. Two caveats are structural and carried into every step: (1) the counts come from salmon as delivered with no statement of whether the length correction occurred and no quant.sf files or average-transcript-length table in the inputs, so the model is fitted on the counts as delivered with no length offset and the report must state that the length offset is lost and that isoform-usage shifts can appear as differential expression (R-0169@18ab); (2) with 3 replicates per design cell the interaction term — a difference of differences — has low power, so absence from the significant list is not evidence of a shared time trend (R-0063@6190, R-0017@8a47). No enrichment step is planned: the question asks for genes, not pathways.

DESeq2 likelihood ratio test against reduced model ~ condition + time

DESeq2 interaction/time-course report with trajectory clusters
Low count filter: keep a gene with at least 10 counts in at least the smallest group size of samples
DESeq2 likelihood ratio test against reduced model ~ condition + time

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

With two or three replicates per group, the design step states the expected power of the test before the model. The tools of record for a power and sample size calculation, RNASeqPower and PROPER, are not in the pool here. Compute the power from the closed form of the sample size in terms of the depth, the biological coefficient of variation, the fold change, and the significance level, or take the dispersion from a pilot or a public dataset of the same tissue, and state the fold change that the design can find with 80 percent power. State that a larger replicate count raises the power more than a deeper sequencing does. The statement is a caution on the plan and not a reason to loosen the threshold.

With an interaction question and three or fewer replicates in a cell of the design, the interaction term has low power. The interaction coefficient is a difference of two differences, thus its standard error is larger than the standard error of a main effect at the same replicate number. Keep the interaction test as the primary result, but report the simple effects in each level beside it, with the same threshold. State the power limit in the report, and do not loosen the threshold to compensate. A gene that is absent from the interaction list is not shown to have the same effect in both levels.

If the smallest group holds three replicates, the test has low power. Both count models find only a small share of the true differentially expressed genes, most of them with a large fold change. Interpret the result with caution, and state the power limit in the report. Keep alpha at its default value, and do not change the threshold to compensate for the small design. A gene that is not in the list is not shown to be unchanged.
